## Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Pairwise training margins measure local score separation. They cannot establish whether recent intent improves recommendation ranks. (2) Left padding can affect recurrent states even with zero padding embeddings. Padding correctness must precede behavioral interpretation. (3) Feedback identifies weak immediate relevance and possible redundancy. Available histories and descriptions support proxies, while compatibility, ownership and mood often remain unknown.

**Related-work insights.** (1) Betello et al. motivate comparing recent and older interaction removal [1]. Their training perturbations do not establish effects for frozen-model inference. (2) *Does It Look Sequential?* motivates history-shuffle controls for GRU4Rec [2]. Sensitivity becomes useful evidence only when paired with target-ranking outcomes. (3) Krichene and Rendle show that sampled metrics can misrepresent full-catalog performance [3]. Diagnostic ranking scopes must therefore remain explicit.

These insights define three directions: recurrent correctness, useful temporal dependence, and evidence-grounded feedback interpretation.

## Framework

| Layer | Measurement | Interpretation boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Correctness | Padding-invariance error | Implementation validity |
| Temporal behavior | Paired ranks after history edits | Model dependence, not causal intent |
| Feedback grounding | Supported/contradicted/unknown evidence | No inferred ownership or mood |
| Selection | Host macro validation HR@10 | Sole model-selection objective |

## Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means more implementation work.

1. **Padding-invariance gate — 3/8/2.** Compare identical histories with different padding. Originality: established technique, but family-specific application; potential: prevents misleading experiments, but adds no preference signal; difficulty: few checks, but recurrent fixes require predictor parity. Reference: PyTorch GRU equations [4].
2. **Paired temporal-utility adapter — 5/8/4.** Compare recent deletion, older deletion and prefix shuffling on fixed training-prefix targets. Originality: useful integration, but established perturbations; potential: tests actionable hypotheses, but cannot guarantee validation gains; difficulty: reuses ModelView, but requires careful batching and uncertainty estimates. References: [1–3].
3. **Evidence-grounded feedback rubric — 5/6/5.** Annotate recent alignment, possible redundancy and identity clarity. Originality: task-specific synthesis, but familiar annotation principles; potential: improves feedback interpretation, but twenty users provide limited evidence; difficulty: simple schema, but independent annotation takes effort.

## Selected idea: Paired temporal-utility adapter

At 0% progress, prioritize a measurable diagnostic before introducing architectural complexity. Freeze each category’s single GRU4Rec and construct held-out next-item targets from training histories only. Keep each target and candidate set identical across original and perturbed histories; exclude empty-history comparisons.

```text
verify padding invariance and final-nonpadding readout
for each training-prefix target:
    score original, recent-deleted, older-deleted histories
    score shuffled prefix with final item preserved
    record paired target ranks and top-10 overlap
aggregate by category, prefix length and target popularity
bootstrap users; emit metrics, definitions and uncertainty
```

Preserve `DiagnosisProbe(view, device)`, `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` and `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis)`. Report missing observations as unavailable. Treat temporal sensitivity as a hypothesis generator; select subsequent single-model interventions exclusively through the unchanged host validation protocol.

idea.description: Extend the family-aware GRU4Rec diagnostic adapter with padding checks and paired history perturbations that measure whether recent interactions and ordering help rank training-prefix targets.
idea.motivation: Current margin and geometry probes cannot distinguish useful temporal dependence from broad historical relevance. Qualitative feedback motivates testing this distinction, but does not establish its cause. Early research progress favors a small, interpretable diagnostic extension.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain all four category routes and exactly one independently trained GRU4Rec checkpoint per category. Use only training histories to construct diagnostic prefixes and next-item targets; exclude those targets from every perturbed input. Use seed 42 for reproducible diagnostic sampling. Compare equal-sized recent and older deletions with matched retained lengths; shuffle only the prefix while retaining the final observed item. Preserve chronological order after deletion and restore left padding. Check inference in eval mode against unpadded single-history execution; read the maximum nonpadding index, never count-1. If padding affects recurrence, skip padded updates or compact valid sequences and update the embedded predictor writer identically. Preserve ModelView.log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items), including B x L x 2 candidate scoring. Keep the required loader contract and existing valid-position margin probes. Add training-prefix metrics with explicit counts, ranking scope, perturbation definitions and user-cluster uncertainty. Do not access unavailable category metadata, review text, ratings or latent simulator traits. Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Keep artifacts under the trial directory and bound diagnostic computation within the shared budget. No measured improvement is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    preserve model mode; enter eval and inference mode
    metrics = existing_family_compatible_margin_probes(train_loader)
    prefixes = reproducible_training_only_prefix_targets(view.user_train, seed=42)
    metrics.padding = compare_padding_variants_and_unpadded_execution(prefixes)
    if padding check fails:
        return measured_metrics_and_failure_definitions_without_behavioral_claims()
    for user, history, target in prefixes:
        variants = matched_nonempty_deletions_and_prefix_shuffle(history)
        candidates = fixed_training_only_candidate_set(history, target)
        for variant in [history] + variants:
            features = view.log2feats(left_pad(variant))
            final = gather_maximum_nonpadding_position(features, variant)
            scores = view.predict_score(final, candidates)
            record_target_rank_and_top10(user, variant, scores)
    aggregate_paired_changes_with_counts_by_category_length_popularity()
    bootstrap_users_preserving_all_their_prefixes()
    restore model mode
    return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    embed measured metrics and definitions
    request evidence-linked findings, uncertainty and testable hypotheses
    prohibit causal-intent claims and unsupported metadata assumptions

originality.positive: Combines recurrent correctness checks, matched history edits and target-ranking outcomes within the existing family-specific diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: The individual perturbation and paired-evaluation techniques are established; novelty lies mainly in their integration.

future_potential.positive: Could guide controlled GRU4Rec interventions by separating padding artifacts, recent-item dependence and broader ordering effects.
future_potential.negative: Training-prefix findings may not generalize to validation users or identify a change that improves the pinned HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the existing trained model and scoring interfaces without adding a second predictor or requiring retraining.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct prefix construction, matched perturbations, batched scoring and clustered uncertainty require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Betello et al.: sequential recommendation perturbation study
contributions: Motivates studying sensitivity to interaction removal and position.
Introduces Finite Rank-Biased Overlap for finite recommendation lists.
limitations: Training-data perturbation findings do not directly establish effects of fixed-model inference edits.
Recommendation-list changes alone do not establish improved target ranking or current user intent.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential?
contributions: Studies original versus shuffled histories, including GRU4Rec.
Combines recommendation accuracy and recommendation-set comparisons.
limitations: Sensitivity alone does not prove useful sequential reasoning.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics.
Motivates explicitly identifying the candidate scope of diagnostic measurements.
limitations: Does not justify changing this task's pinned host evaluator.
Does not identify which GRU4Rec intervention will improve the benchmark.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU documentation
contributions: Specifies recurrent equations showing that zero inputs need not leave hidden states unchanged.
Provides the implementation basis for testing padding invariance.
limitations: Documentation is not empirical evidence of a padding bug in the supplied model.
Padding correctness alone does not establish recommendation quality.
